summary: A flexible Mae Rim day out linking the Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden’s glasshouses and canopy walk with mountain scenery and a meal around Mon Cham. It is a suggested route, not a single organised attraction; choose a few stops and arrange transport for the whole loop.
whyGo: See a major botanical collection and elevated forest walk, then continue into the cooler Mae Rim highlands.
Mix nature, viewpoints and a relaxed local meal in one outing outside Chiang Mai city.
December falls within the October–February period the Tourism Authority of Thailand recommends for Mon Cham.
bestFor: Visitors wanting a flexible nature day with both managed gardens and mountain scenery
Small groups or families who can hire a car and driver or self-drive
Travellers comfortable with winding roads, uneven outdoor paths and variable weather
skipIf: You need a reliable public-transport connection between the garden and hill viewpoints.
You need a fully step-free route or guaranteed clear mountain views.
You prefer a fixed itinerary with one transparent all-in price.
duration: Planning estimate: 6–8 hours from Chiang Mai for the botanic garden, a few Mae Rim stops and meal, including road time. The garden alone can take 2–4 hours because it covers a large, hilly site; add time for traffic and the climb to Mon Cham.
cost: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden’s Tourism Authority of Thailand listing states ฿50 adult admission and free entry for children under 12. Transport, garden shuttle/attraction extras, food and any Mon Cham activity or viewpoint charges are additional; no single loop fare was verified. Recheck garden charges before December 2026.
hours: The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden as open daily 08:30–17:00. Mon Cham has no single verified visitor-hours listing; viewpoints, restaurants and seasonal attractions may set their own hours. Confirm current access before setting out.
bestTime: Start early to give the garden and mountain drive daylight, and to improve the chance of seeing morning mist around Mon Cham. TAT describes October–February as the best period there. December is busy in Chiang Mai, and fog, rain or haze can still affect views.
gettingThere: The garden and Mon Cham are north-west of Chiang Mai in Mae Rim. TAT describes Mon Cham as about 40 minutes from central Chiang Mai and recommends travelling by car; it notes the final roads include lateritic dirt track. A hired car and driver is the simplest way to combine stops and wait between them. No dependable public-transport link for the full loop was verified. Allow extra time for winding roads and holiday traffic.
booking: The loop itself has no central booking. Check the botanic garden’s current ticket and facility notices, and arrange a driver or rental car in advance for December. Contact individual Mon Cham venues directly if you want a meal, activity or overnight stay; do not assume their services are included in a day-trip quote.
accessibility: The garden is set on hilly terrain and the overall loop requires vehicle transfers. A canopy walk and greenhouse visits involve walking; step-free access, accessible shuttle availability and toilet provision across the route were not confirmed. Mon Cham’s uneven and sometimes unpaved uphill roads may limit mobility access. Ask the garden and chosen venues about the exact route before travelling.
practicalTips: Agree the stops, waiting time, return time and total driver cost before leaving Chiang Mai.
Prioritise the garden and one or two hill stops rather than trying to cover every Mae Rim attraction.
Bring a light warm layer for the hills, sun and rain protection, water and shoes suitable for walking.
Carry cash for small purchases and any fees not included in transport.
Check road and weather conditions on the day; avoid assuming a viewpoint will have mist or clear skies.
decemberNotes: December is within Mon Cham’s stated cool-season window and is a popular time to visit Chiang Mai. The garden ran a Botanic Festival from 24 December 2025 to 4 January 2026, but that was a past event and does not confirm dates or programming for December 2026. Expect extra traffic around Christmas and New Year; no 2026 event schedule or special hours were verified.
uncertainties: This is a suggested route rather than a formal attraction or fixed operator itinerary; exact stops depend on the traveller and day.
The garden’s posted hours and tariff are from its Tourism Authority of Thailand listing; reconfirm close to travel.
Current Mon Cham admission or activity charges, restaurant hours and road conditions were not established.
Accessibility details and December 2026 festival dates or closures remain unverified.
